narrative.overview:
Amber is a piece of rhodonite: dense graphite stone with one pink vein running through it. The stone is everything you see at rest: graphite page, a slightly lighter graphite card, quiet gray words. The vein is pastel pink, and it only shows where something matters right now: the one main action, the box you just ticked, the words your search found, the thing that has focus. Hold the interface and it should feel calm, cool and solid, with color reserved for meaning.

It is a working surface, used daily and quickly, so density is moderate and the hierarchy is plain: a page heading, sections marked by a thin colored edge, and rows of tasks. Personality lives in small tactile moments rather than in decoration: a round checkbox whose tick draws itself in, a row that lifts into a card under the pointer, an Undo message that slides up from the bottom. Everything has a reduced-motion version that simply appears.

Dark is the default stone (the `:root` values); light mode is the same stone in daylight, chosen by the system, with the pink line deepened to deep rose and focus drawn in graphite so both stay visible on white.

- Graphite and off-white, with a single pink accent that always means something. - Flat surfaces separated by tone and hairline borders; shadows only on what floats. - Pills for actions, soft corners for containers, round for anything ticked. - One typeface, Plus Jakarta Sans, at a small set of sizes and weights. - Every control has an edge people can find (3:1), and every color meets level AA in both modes.

rules.name: The One Vein Rule
rules.body: Pink marks one kind of thing at a time: the primary action, the ticked state, the found words, or focus. It is never decoration, never a background wash, never a heading color. If a screen has two pink buttons, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Graphite-on-Pink Rule
rules.body: Text on pink is graphite. Pastel pink is never text on a light background.

rules.name: The No Pink Category Rule
rules.body: Pink is not a category color; it would compete with focus and the main action.

rules.name: The 16px on Touch Rule
rules.body: On a touch screen, fields are 16px text, or Safari zooms the page.

rules.name: The Weight Not Size Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy inside the list comes from weight and muted color, not new sizes: a section heading is 0.875rem semibold, not a bigger font.

rules.name: The Wrap, Don't Squeeze Rule
rules.body: Rows and bars use `flex-wrap` with minimum widths in rem. At 200% text, move buttons, the Add button and the search field drop to their own line; words are never crushed.

rules.name: The 44px Finger Rule
rules.body: On a coarse pointer every target reaches 44px, through an invisible layer around the control, so the drawing and the layout stay the same size.

rules.name: The Shadow Means Floating Rule
rules.body: Nothing that stays in the page's flow casts a shadow. If it has a shadow, it is modal or transient.

rules.name: The Graphite Chosen Rule
rules.body: Something chosen (a tag on a task, the Any/Open/Done switch) fills with the text color and shows a check. Pink stays for ticked, found, focused and the main action.

dos: Do take every color from the tokens in `src/app.css`; both modes are defined there.
Do keep pink to one meaning per moment, with graphite text on it and deep rose for pink lines in light mode.
Do give every control a 3:1 edge (`control-edge`) and every target 44px on touch.
Do separate surfaces by tone and hairline; add a shadow only to something that floats.
Do pair every transition with `motion-reduce` so it appears instantly instead.
Do use Tailwind classes; inline styles and `data:` URLs are blocked by the Content-Security-Policy.
donts: Don't use pink as text on a light background, as decoration, or as a category color.
Don't use black (`#000000`) for text or surfaces; graphite is `#2b2b2b`.
Don't add a second typeface or load fonts from another domain.
Don't put shadows on cards, rows or anything in the page's flow.
Don't squeeze rows at large text; let them wrap.
Don't use category colors as fills behind text.
Don't redraw, recolor or stretch the Itrium logo files; they are copies from the brand assets.
